title: Why doubling hides, then surprises
body: A tumour is a lump of cells.
Cells make new cells by dividing. One cell splits into two, two become four, and so on.
Cancer cells don't stop dividing when there are enough of them. So they keep doubling.
Doubling starts slowly. 8 cells become 16. Later, 8,000 become 16,000 in the same time.
So for a long time the cluster looks tiny. Then it seems to grow all of a sudden.
Screening looks for signs of cancer in people with no symptoms, before they are noticeable. Cancer may be easier to treat when it is found early.
realWorld: When cancer is found at an early stage, treatment is more likely to be successful.
model: This is a teaching model. Its months and doubling times show the idea; they aren't real growth speeds.
